title: Implement Entra ID Integration with ABM for Account Auto Provisioning for Microsoft Intune
author_notes: Shaping note: the solution must support iOS managed iPhones for Corporate-Owned (COD), BYOD, and Shared Device scenarios.

Effort tier: T4 (identity-plane integration across Microsoft Entra ID + Apple Business Manager + Intune: federated authentication, SCIM auto-provisioning of Managed Apple IDs, and three enrollment models; org-wide change to Apple sign-in, higher risk).

Scope: Entra ID <-> ABM Federated Authentication + automatic Managed Apple ID provisioning (SCIM from Entra to ABM and/or just-in-time on first federated sign-in), then leveraged for COD (account-driven/ADE device enrollment), BYOD (account-driven user enrollment), and Shared (no-user-affinity + Managed Apple ID). ABM console internals deferred to Apple documentation. version_directive: New; branding: off (white-label).
hook: Federate Entra ID with Apple Business Manager so Managed Apple IDs provision themselves — and every iPhone enrolls the right way
problem: Managed Apple IDs are the backbone of modern iPhone management, but creating and maintaining them by hand — and reconciling them with your real users — is a slog, and it blocks the cleanest enrollment experiences. The fix is to integrate Microsoft Entra ID with Apple Business Manager: federate authentication so users sign in to Apple services with their Entra credentials, and auto-provision Managed Apple IDs from Entra (SCIM) so accounts simply exist when you need them. With that foundation in place, all three iPhone models — Corporate-Owned, BYOD, and Shared — enroll into Microsoft Intune the right way. This solution sets up the federation and auto-provisioning, then wires each enrollment scenario on top.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — how Entra ID ↔ Apple Business Manager federation works, automatic Managed Apple ID provisioning (SCIM from Entra plus just-in-time on first federated sign-in), how this enables the three iOS enrollment models, and the domain-capture / existing-Apple-ID conflict considerations.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Entra ID with the rights to federate + provision, Apple Business Manager, verified domain(s), the Apple MDM Push (APNs) certificate, the ADE enrollment token, Intune, user/group scoping, a pilot group) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: federate ABM with Entra ID, configure SCIM auto-provisioning of Managed Apple IDs (scoped to a pilot group first), resolve any existing-Apple-ID conflicts, then stand up enrollment for each model — Corporate-Owned (account-driven / ADE device enrollment), BYOD (account-driven user enrollment), and Shared (no-user-affinity with Managed Apple IDs) — then pilot, validate, and expand.

Per-scenario guidance — how the federated identity + Managed Apple ID flows into each model (COD vs BYOD vs Shared), what the end-user sign-in experience looks like, and how to keep them cleanly separated by group.

5 PowerShell scripts — federation/provisioning readiness discovery, per-user Managed-Apple-ID + per-device enrollment-model validation, a fleet provisioning-coverage and scenario-breakdown report, safe remediation (re-provision / fix scope), and a provisioning + enrollment scope-group builder for the three scenarios.
short: Integrate Microsoft Entra ID with Apple Business Manager — federated authentication + automatic Managed Apple ID provisioning (SCIM) — then enroll iPhones the right way for Corporate-Owned, BYOD, and Shared scenarios in Microsoft Intune. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
